behavior_anomalies.why: The run begins with four flu patients while functional ventilators are zero, but never records that patients cannot be ventilated, any triage or denial decision, or an order for additional ventilators. The patient population continues growing without any observable consequence of the zero ventilator resource.

The run begins accumulating flu patients despite zero available ventilators, but never records any consequence for patients who would depend on ventilatory support—such as denial, triage, transfer, deterioration, or death. Subsequent patient accumulation likewise proceeds without any modeled effect of the zero resource.

The hospital is specified as having 40 beds, yet the patient count rises from 39 to 47 without any departures, transfers, diversion, or other capacity-expanding action. Subsequent arrivals continue increasing the count far beyond the hospital's capacity.

The hospital is specified as having 40 beds, but the logged patient count exceeds that capacity without any diversion, transfer, discharge, overflow, or other capacity consequence. The patient count then continues increasing far beyond 40.

The recorded patient count jumps beyond the hospital's 40-bed capacity, but the log shows no overflow, transfer, refusal, or other capacity-limiting consequence. The same unbounded accumulation continues thereafter.

action admit-flu-patients-v1 refuses up front with check 'the hospital has enough available beds' on actor.components.hospital_capacity.available_beds, a stock the actor's own activity consumes. Fix with three changes: (1) the action only STARTS the activity (sets a status such as 'driving'), with no check on that stock and no progress or consumption effects; (2) add a process that, every tick while the status is active and the stock is above zero, makes one tick of progress and consumes the stock; (3) add a process that switches the status to a stopped/failed value when the stock is at or below zero, so the actor discovers it by observation.
